# Circular nutrient loops from aquaculture and urban wastewater in the Nordics

## Scope and evidence rules

This is a bounded research dataset, not an essay. I prioritised primary sources from SINTEF, NIBIO, Mattilsynet, Fiskeridirektoratet, Miljødirektoratet, NSVA/RecoLab, Helsingborg city material, and peer-reviewed or thesis work directly tied to operating systems. I separate **fact**, **inference**, **secondary mention**, **not found**, and **disproved/unsupported**. Negative findings are explicit because, for this case, missing public data is itself material. citeturn25view2turn25view3turn41search0turn41search3turn8view1turn13view0

For aquaculture statistics, the closest authoritative open statistical backbone is **Fiskeridirektoratet’s statistics bank**, which supports API and CSV export. It is authoritative for aquaculture production context, but I did **not** find an official open national API/CSV that directly publishes Norway-wide annual N/P discharge totals from aquaculture; those totals are published in reports/models instead. citeturn41search0turn41search1turn41search3

The strongest primary numbers I found are these: SINTEF’s 2019 national mass-balance estimate of about **66.4 kt N** and **14 kt P**, HI/TEOTIL’s **2018 dissolved** emissions of **51.5 kt N** and **6.845 kt P**, and the older Wang-based feed-balance estimate that about **62% of feed N** and **70% of feed P** are emitted. These are **not the same metric** and should not be blended: one pair is total national discharge, one pair is dissolved nutrients only, and one pair is a feed-balance share. citeturn33search1turn29search1turn34search1turn34search7turn30search2

The regulatory picture is therefore asymmetric: open-net marine farming is regulated mainly through standardised sea-aquaculture conditions and monitoring, while **capture/use** of solids is operationally much more developed in **land-based** systems. On the product side, fish sludge can enter fertiliser value chains only under strict raw-material, hygiene, contaminant, registration and market-access conditions, and marine-origin sludge is harder than freshwater sludge. citeturn25view1turn28view0turn25view3turn22search9turn22search13turn22search4

The robust primary picture is that **RecoLab is operational**, receives source-separated flows from Oceanhamnen, and has published **process-level** recovery evidence, but I did **not** find public primary documents with realised annual district-wide **tonnes of recovered N, P and K**. The best public numbers are therefore per-PE/day balances and technology-level recovery percentages, not a municipal annual production statement. citeturn8view1turn8view2turn9view3turn13view0turn13view2

## Short verdict and controls

The short verdict is this: **the circularity case is stronger for land-based aquaculture sludge and for source-separated blackwater than for open-net marine sludge today; stronger for field-applied fertiliser products than for commercial hydroponic nutrient substitution; and much stronger for “technical potential” than for “realised annual recovery”.** Norway has credible primary quantification of aquaculture nutrient losses to sea, but weak public primary reporting on realised sludge capture/use by end-market. Helsingborg RecoLab is real, operating, and unusually transparent, but public evidence still stops short of a clean municipal dashboard stating “X tonnes N, Y tonnes P, Z tonnes K recovered this year”. Nordic aquaponics exists, yet public primary evidence for routine municipal-blackwater-to-hydroponics loops remains sparse. citeturn33search1turn34search7turn25view3turn13view0turn13view2turn17search1turn39search2

### Do-not-say list

Do **not** say “70% of the feed goes into the fjord” as a settled fact. The available primary/public numbers are metric-specific and non-equivalent: feed-balance shares, dissolved-only model outputs, and national total discharge estimates are different constructs. citeturn30search2turn34search1turn33search1

Do **not** say RecoLab currently recovers a published annual district-wide tonnage of **N, P and K**. I did not find that primary statement. The safe wording is that RecoLab has published process balances and pilot recovery percentages, while district-wide annual N/P/K output in tonnes is still a public-data gap. citeturn13view0turn13view2

Do **not** say Nordic hydroponics is inherently circular because much Nordic greenhouse production is hydroponic already. The key issue here is whether **waste-derived nutrients** are substituted in safely, legally and economically; the public evidence base for that remains limited. citeturn39search2turn25view3

Do **not** say fish-sludge fertiliser can straightforwardly be exported as a CE-marked fertiliser to the EU/EEA. Mattilsynet states that fish sludge is not currently an allowed raw material for CE-marked fertilisers under EU 2019/1009, and marine fish sludge needs permission even before that. citeturn22search13turn25view3
